editorial_candidates.rationale: The ItemBody gives two explicit, contrasting colored crystal neighborhoods from the same shape. A paired local graph would make the changed color-1 versus color-2 arrows under the restricted symmetric model immediately visible; the action tables and prose are already clear, so this is not a rendering defect.

concrete_maps_and_relations.quantum_group: Use (2,1) as center; f_0:(2,1)->(2,2), f_1:(2,1)->(2,1,1), and e_1:(2,1)->(1,1), equivalently f_1:(1,1)->(2,1); colors 2 have no incident crystal arrow at the center.
concrete_maps_and_relations.restricted_symmetric: Use M_(2,1) as center; f_0:M_(2,1)->M_(2,2), f_2:M_(2,1)->M_(3,1), and e_2:M_(2,1)->M_(2), equivalently f_2:M_(2)->M_(2,1); colors 1 have no incident crystal arrow at the center.
concrete_maps_and_relations.convention: Orient every crystal edge in the f_i direction and label it by i; use separate panels. Do not put the ordinary Chevalley coefficient q^-1 on these normalized crystal edges.

editorial_candidates.diagram_math_checked: Arrow endpoints and vanishing colors match Statement lines 43–46 and the detailed signature computations at Verification line 72.
